title: Marcus's Penne alla Vodka
description: My favorite dish to cook — a silky tomato-cream sauce with just enough vodka to make it sing. Restaurant-quality, ready in about the time it takes to boil the pasta.
prep_notes: The alcohol cooks off — this won't make anyone tipsy. Use good tomato paste and freshly grated Parmesan for the best result.

steps.title: Boil the pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the penne until just shy of al dente — it'll finish in the sauce. Before draining, scoop out a cup of the pasta water and set it aside.

steps.title: Build the aromatic base
steps.text: While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil and butter in a large high-sided skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 4-5 minutes. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook one more minute — don't let it brown.

steps.title: Toast the tomato paste
steps.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook, stirring often, until it deepens in color and smells rich and sweet, about 2-3 minutes. This step is what gives the sauce its depth.

steps.title: Add the vodka
steps.text: Pour in the vodka and stir. Let it simmer and reduce by about half, 3-4 minutes, so the alcohol cooks off and the flavors concentrate.

steps.title: Make it creamy
steps.text: Lower the heat and stir in the heavy cream until the sauce turns a beautiful blush color. Season with the salt and black pepper. Let it gently simmer for a couple of minutes.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.text: Add the drained penne and the grated Parmesan to the sauce, tossing constantly until every piece is coated. Splash in pasta water a little at a time if it needs loosening.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Taste and adjust the salt. Serve right away, topped with torn fresh basil, extra Parmesan, and a few grinds of black pepper.
